newsitem.title: BELGIUM: DUTCH TELFORT TELECOMS VENTURE SEEKING TO GROW.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH TELFORT TELECOMS VENTURE SEEKING TO GROW.

text.p: Dutch telecommunications joint venture Telfort BV said on Monday it expected revenues of 200 million guilders in 1997 and hoped to increase that tenfold within five to seven years.
"We are aiming between now and five years to get 10 to 15 percent of the Dutch market," Koos van der Meulen, Telfort's managing director told reporters.
The Telfort alliance between British Telecommunications Plc and Dutch railway company NS was awarded a licence last October to compete with the former fixed-line monopoly of the Dutch PTT .
Van der Meulen said Telfort's growth expectations would translate into about two billion guilders, given the expected market growth as the European Union's telecoms liberalisation plan moves forward.
He added Telfort already had about 1,500 corporate clients. It expected to announce on Wednesday that it was launching a network linking the critical Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Utrecht "ring".
Van der Meulen said the company expected to employ about 1,200 people within two years, compared with 400 now.

Van der Meulen said it was critical, however, to bring down the fees charged by former Dutch phone monopoly KPN for connecting to its network, which he said were much higher than those in more liberalised markets such as Britain and Sweden.
